# Charlotta

## Overview

- **Age:** Fourteen years old, later a grown-up young lady  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007), [v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042), [v4 c4 P16](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0016)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010)</sub>
- **Role:** handmaiden  <sub>[v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c28 P56](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0056)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Charlotta the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Appearance

Charlotta has a freckled face, a snub nose, and a exceptionally wide smile. In her youth, she braided her hair in innumerable plaits with prominent blue bows. Upon growing into young ladyhood, she discarded the blue bows and styled her hair in an enormous pompadour.

_Sources: [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011), [v2 c30 P13](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0013), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007), [v4 c3 P37](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0037)_

## Personality

Charlotta is a warm-hearted, cheerful, and faithful individual who is intensely loyal to her mistress. She possesses a brisk, energetic manner when performing tasks and never lets on if she thinks her mistress's imaginative play is silly. She prefers the honest company of Prince Edward Island to life elsewhere and retains her sincere affection for her friends over the years.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P22](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0022), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c28 P56](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0056), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011), [v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010), [v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000)_

- To serve and support Miss Lavendar faithfully  <sub>[v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043)</sub>

## History

Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge as a fourteen-year-old handmaiden to Miss Lavendar Lewis, taking her board and clothes as the fourth sister in her family to serve the household. She developed a deep affection for Miss Lavendar and welcomed guests like Anne Shirley and Diana Barry with great cheerfulness. When Miss Lavendar prepared to marry Stephen Irving, Charlotta assisted enthusiastically with the wedding preparations before moving with the newlyweds to Boston. Though initially homesick in Boston and preferring Prince Edward Island, she returned with the Irvings to Echo Lodge during subsequent summers. She later married a good-tempered bricklayer named Tom, and eventually attended Anne Shirley's wedding, where she happily threw rice and old shoes for the bride and groom.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010), [v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042), [v4 c4 P16](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- Her real name is Leonora Bowman  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Youngest of the Bowman sisters who served Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Given the nickname 'Charlotta the Fourth' by Miss Lavendar to distinguish her from her sisters  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Moved to Boston with Mr. and Mrs. Irving after their wedding  <sub>[v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048)</sub>
- Married an American bricklayer named Tom  <sub>[v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m real glad of that. They said I did at home, but I thought likely they just wanted to aggravate me. I don’t want no Yankee accent. Not that I’ve a word to say against the Yankees, Miss Shirley, ma’am. They’re real civilized. But give me old P.E. Island every time.  <sub>[v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010)</sub>

> Goodness, no, Miss Shirley, ma’am. I wouldn’t know who he meant if he did. Of course, when we got married he had to say, 'I take thee, Leonora,’ and I declare to you, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’ve had the most dreadful feeling ever since that it wasn’t me he was talking to and I haven’t been rightly married at all. And so you’re going to be married yourself, Miss Shirley, ma’am? I always thought I’d like to marry a doctor. It would be so handy when the children had measles and croup. Tom is only a bricklayer, but he’s real good-tempered. When I said to him, says I, 'Tom, can I go to Miss Shirley’s wedding? I mean to go anyhow, but I’d like to have your consent,’ he just says, 'Suit yourself, Charlotta, and you’ll suit me.’ That’s a real pleasant kind of husband to have, Miss Shirley, ma’am.  <sub>[v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042)</sub>
